name: stage
title: Stage
description: Gamestage UI arranged around a scene the host owns. The scene is a Three.js canvas, a Unity build, a video, a static image or somebody else's embed, and stage never renders it, never reaches into it, never measures it and never assumes it exists: it takes the node and puts it on the page untouched. Three decisions carry the component. The scene sits in normal flow and every other layer is absolute over it, so the scene gives the stage its box and the stage sets no width, no height and no aspect-ratio of its own. Layers pinned to an edge are as big as their contents while `behind`, `overlay` and `celebration` cover the stage, which is what makes the pointer rule expressible: `data-gs-pointer` is `none` on every covering layer, so a press falls through to the scene, and `auto` on the edge layers, which can only swallow a press inside themselves. And `data-gs-safe-area` holds the layers clear of a phone's notch and home bar by default, so a host that has already padded for the insets can say so rather than paying them twice.
docs: Pass the scene as `scene` and the library's own layers as `Stage.Layer` children: `<Stage scene={<canvas/>}><Stage.Layer layer="hud" placement="top"><Hud …/></Stage.Layer></Stage>`. `layer` is the closed set `scene`, `behind`, `hud`, `overlay`, `nav`, `celebration` and decides the stacking order, which belongs to the library. `placement` pins an edge layer; a layer with no placement covers the stage. `pointer` overrules the default when the host knows better, which is the case a modal overlay needs: pass `pointer="auto"` on an overlay meant to block the scene. Omitting `scene` is supported and renders no scene layer at all, because a quiz with nothing behind it uses the same components as a Unity build; the host's container then gives the stage its height. Pass `safeArea={false}` only when the host has already padded for the device's insets. Stage depends on tokens alone: bds.md's dependency table lists it against `hud`, which is what the reference screen composes rather than what the component imports, and a stage that imported a HUD could not be the thing a host puts its own components into.
